q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID , ROUND((SUM(EXPERIENCE_YEARS) / COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID)),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY PROJECT_ID ORDER BY PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 calculates the average experience years for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of employees in that project. Q2, on the other hand, calculates the average experience years for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of projects that each employee is part of. This difference in the denominator leads to potentially different results.
counterexample_dsp: A project with two employees where one employee has 10 years of experience and the other has 0 years of experience. The average calculated by Q1 will be (10 + 0) / 2 = 5, while the average calculated by Q2 will be (10 + 0) / 1 = 10, assuming each employee is only part of one project.
